original_question: In the two-server queue case m = 2 with stationary waiting time D, when the load satisfies rho = 1 and the service-time distribution is subexponential (for example regularly varying), what is the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Conjecture 1.1: the open problem on the exact tail asymptotics of the stationary waiting time in the critical-load GI/GI/2 FCFS queue with heavy-tailed service times, read together with the nearby clarifying statements Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly isolates the paper's main critical-case ingredients: the two-server setting (m = 2), the stationary waiting time D, the critical load rho = 1, the subexponential/heavy-tail regime for service times, and the request for large-x asymptotics of P(D > x).
missing_details: The paper's model is specifically a GI/GI/2 first-come first-served queue, not just an unspecified two-server queue.
The primitives should be stated explicitly: i.i.d. interarrival times with mean a and i.i.d. service times with distribution B and mean b.
The load is defined by rho = b/a; thus rho = 1 means the critical case b = a inside the still-stable two-server regime.
D should be identified as the stationary waiting time of an arriving customer under the FCFS discipline.
The paper treats this as the unresolved boundary case between the already understood regimes rho < 1 and 1 < rho < 2; that contextual role is implicit in your draft but not stated.
The official formulation asks for the exact tail asymptotics/equivalent, not merely a rough order estimate.

The nearby context distinguishes general subexponential assumptions from the regularly varying special case handled more explicitly in Theorem 1.3; your draft mentions regular variation only as an example, but not its role in the paper.
The paper's notation uses the service-time law B (and nearby results also use the residual service-time law), which should be named to make the question fully stand-alone.
refined_question: Let D be the stationary waiting time in a stable GI/GI/2 first-come first-served queue with i.i.d. interarrival times of mean a and i.i.d. service times with distribution B and mean b, and let rho = b/a. In the critical-load case rho = 1 (so b = a), assuming that the service-time distribution B is subexponential, determine the exact asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x -> infinity; in particular, what is the corresponding exact tail asymptotic in the regularly varying case singled out in the paper?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper's first open problem on rare events in multi-server queues: the unresolved critical-load (rho = 1) tail asymptotics for the stationary waiting time in the two-server FCFS queue. Conjecture 1.1 is the nearest official formulation, while Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 provide the nearby sharpening and the regularly varying special-case context that make the notation and scope precise. I therefore kept the question narrowly on the GI/GI/2 FCFS critical case, without broadening it to m-server systems, moment questions, or the already treated rho < 1 and 1 < rho < 2 regimes.
